props.label: Removal, cutting and pruning
props.html:
What we do

Removal, cutting and pruning

We handle unwanted or risky trees — full removal, cutting back, and pruning to shape or reduce a canopy — and we clear the mess when we're done.

On bush-fringe blocks, keeping trees back from the house is part of sensible defendable space. Some tree work needs council approval or a permit; we'll flag anything that does before we start.

Get a free quote

What's included

  • Tree removal
  • Cutting and canopy reduction
  • Pruning and shaping
  • Green-waste and debris cleared
  • Advice on council approval where needed
  • Fixed-price quote, no call-out fee

props.label: Tree services FAQs
props.html:
Good to know

Tree services FAQs

Which landscaping suits a bushfire-prone block?
On bush-fringe blocks near Dharawal or the Georges River, we plan defendable space: low-flammability planting away from the house, non-combustible hardscaping close in, and clear separation from bushland. We work to the intent of Planning for Bush Fire Protection. Check your BAL rating with the RFS and council.
Do I need council approval for landscaping?
Many jobs like turf, garden beds and paving need no approval. Bigger retaining walls, structures near boundaries, or tree removal can need a development application or a permit. We flag anything that does before we start and can prepare council-ready plans. Confirm specifics with Campbelltown Council.
Are you licensed and insured?
Yes, we are a licensed contractor, licence number 353-827-C. We are happy to show our credentials before any work starts, so you know exactly who is on your property.
